lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: finding qualified help rather than guessing

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic finding qualified help rather than guessing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Given five fictional scenarios that sound legal, civic, financial, or medical in nature, the learner identifies the category of qualified professional or official source appropriate for each (without diagnosing, advising, or predicting an outcome) and writes why guessing or asking a random source would be risky specifically for that scenario.
safetyNotes: This lesson never provides medical, legal, financial, or immigration advice — it teaches which category of qualified source to seek, not what the answer is.
All five scenarios are fictional; no real personal legal, financial, civic, or medical situation needs to be disclosed.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Honestly, which of the four categories (legal, civic, financial, medical) would you personally be most tempted to just guess about instead of asking a qualified source? Why?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Source-category matching: All five scenarios are matched to a plausible, specific category of qualified source. | Boundary discipline: Every response stays within naming a source category and the risk of guessing. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write one additional fictional scenario of their own that deliberately blends two categories (for example, a situation that's both financial and legal), and explain how they'd decide which qualified source to start with.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic finding qualified help rather than guessing task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: finding qualified help rather than guessing worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Given five fictional scenarios that sound legal, civic, financial, or medical in nature, the learner identifies the category of qualified professional or official source appropriate for each (without diagnosing, advising, or predicting an outcome) and writes why guessing or asking a random source would be risky specifically for that scenario.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact finding qualified help rather than guessing decision or action.
Model move 2: Before matching, name a time (real or hypothetical) someone you know asked the wrong kind of source for help.
Model move 3: Match each of the five fictional scenarios to the correct category of qualified source.

Model check: Source-category matching: All five scenarios are matched to a plausible, specific category of qualified source. | Boundary discipline: Every response stays within naming a source category and the risk of guessing.

resources.title: finding qualified help rather than guessing action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for finding qualified help rather than guessing.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: finding qualified help rather than guessing coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Given five fictional scenarios that sound legal, civic, financial, or medical in nature, the learner identifies the category of qualified professional or official source appropriate for each (without diagnosing, advising, or predicting an outcome) and writes why guessing or asking a random source would be risky specifically for that scenario.
Coach direction: Before matching, name a time (real or hypothetical) someone you know asked the wrong kind of source for help.
Learner prompt: Can you think of a time — yours or someone else's, real or hypothetical — when the wrong kind of source was asked for help with something important? What went wrong?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: finding qualified help rather than guessing complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Match each of the five fictional scenarios to the correct category of qualified source.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I matched all five scenarios to a category of qualified professional or official source.
Response 2 (t2-p2): None of my responses attempt to actually answer the scenario's underlying question myself.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: finding qualified help rather than guessing minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Honestly, which of the four categories (legal, civic, financial, medical) would you personally be most tempted to just guess about instead of asking a qualified source? Why?

Success checks: Source-category matching: All five scenarios are matched to a plausible, specific category of qualified source. | Boundary discipline: Every response stays within naming a source category and the risk of guessing.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: finding qualified help rather than guessing supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional finding qualified help rather than guessing condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Source-category matching: All five scenarios are matched to a plausible, specific category of qualified source. | Boundary discipline: Every response stays within naming a source category and the risk of guessing..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g12-u04-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
